mcqs.question: What is the definition of power in physics?

options.A: The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
options.B: The total amount of work done.
options.C: The force applied over a distance.

mcqs.answer: The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
mcqs.explanation: Power measures how quickly work is performed or energy is transferred. It is defined as the rate of doing work, i.e., work done per unit time. Option A states this definition correctly; the other options describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: A person lifts a 20 kg box through a height of 5 m in 2 s. What is the power output? (Take g = 10 m s⁻²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = m g h = 20 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 5 m = 1000 J. Power = work / time = 1000 J / 2 s = 500 W. Hence option B is correct; the other values result from incorrect division or omission of g.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the SI unit "watt"?

options.C: 1 watt equals 1 kilogram metre per second squared.

mcqs.explanation: A watt is defined as one joule of energy transferred per second, directly linking power to energy flow. Option B is the definition of work (joule), C mixes units of force, and D is a unit of pressure.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: A machine does 3000 J of work in 15 s. What is its power?
mcqs.explanation: Power = work / time = 3000 J / 15 s = 200 W. Option B matches this calculation; the other options arise from arithmetic errors.

mcqs.question: Two electric heaters are rated at 1000 W and 1500 W respectively. Which statement is true?

options.A: Both heaters consume the same amount of electrical energy in one hour.
options.B: The 1500 W heater converts more electrical energy to heat per unit time than the 1000 W heater.
options.C: The 1000 W heater will heat a room faster than the 1500 W heater.
options.D: Power rating does not affect heating speed.

mcqs.answer: The 1500 W heater converts more electrical energy to heat per unit time than the 1000 W heater.
mcqs.explanation: Power rating indicates the rate of energy conversion. A 1500 W heater delivers 1500 J each second, which is greater than the 1000 J per second of the 1000 W heater, so it heats faster. Option A is false because energy consumption also depends on time; option C reverses the correct relationship; option D ignores the meaning of power.

mcqs.question: A cyclist climbs a hill, doing 800 J of work in 40 s. What is the cyclist's power?
mcqs.explanation: Power = work / time = 800 J / 40 s = 20 W. Option B is correct; the other options result from mis‑division.

mcqs.question: A student calculates the power of lifting a 10 kg mass through 2 m in 5 s as 20 W by using the formula (mass × distance)/time. Which error has the student made?

options.A: Used mass instead of weight (force) in the work calculation.

mcqs.answer: Used mass instead of weight (force) in the work calculation.
mcqs.explanation: Work = force × distance = (mass × g) × height. The student omitted the factor g, treating mass as force, which halves the work value and yields 20 W instead of the correct 40 W. Options B and C are not the primary mistake, and D is false.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Why is the watt defined as joule per second rather than newton metre per second?

options.A: Because the joule already represents work or energy, linking power directly to energy transfer.
options.B: Because newton metre is a unit of force.
options.C: Because watt is a unit of pressure.
options.D: Because joule per second is a larger unit than newton metre per second.

mcqs.answer: Because the joule already represents work or energy, linking power directly to energy transfer.
mcqs.explanation: A joule is the SI unit of work or energy. Defining power as joule per second directly expresses how much energy is transferred each second. A newton metre is also a joule, so stating newton metre per second would be redundant and less clear. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements about units.
